rejectionGrade: REJECT at 1 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-four attacks run; twenty-three refuted. The one that landed is a custody gap, not an invention: twelve of the sixteen states carry four fleet labels with specific hardware and a machine UDID, and none of that content appears in the only occupancy this corpus pins, nor in either field those twelve states cite. The content is byte-correct against the adopted fleet class — it is the provenance chain that does not reach it.

shouldFix.title: Twelve of sixteen states carry fleet labels, hardware specs and a machine UDID that appear in no document this corpus pins, cited to two fields that demonstrably lack them
shouldFix.where: initialStates[G04.fleet.*] — all twelve — and basedOn, which pins only g04v1
shouldFix.measured: Each of the twelve fleet states opens with one of four labels: 'macos-15 (arm64, 3-core, 7 GB)', 'macos-15-intel (native Intel VM, UDID 4203018E-580F-C1B5-9525-B745CECA79EB)', 'ubuntu-24.04 (x64, 4 CPU, 16 GB)', 'ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64, 4 CPU, 16 GB)'. All four are byte-exact substrings of harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4.json at .harness.fleetClass. None of the four occurs anywhere in G04 v1, which I checked by full-blob search and by enumerating G04 v1's complete path list — it has no fleetClass path and no fleet label at any depth. Its single fleet reference is .harness.matrix, which reads in full 'same D-102 fleet class; --help/--version cold/warm RSS plus one doctor read-only launch per sample'. All twelve states cite 'G04 v1 exactByteIntent and matrix'; I read both cited fields directly and neither contains a label. The subject pins three digests — G04 v1, its review, file 08 — and pins neither G03 v4 nor D-102, so no document in its custody chain carries the content. Three of the eight bare integers in the file (4, 7, 16) exist only inside these unpinned specs.
shouldFix.whyThisIsTheDefect: The count depends on it too. G04 v1's exactByteIntent says 'Per platform: 21 RSS traces for --help, --version, and doctor read-only' and never says how many platforms there are, so the corpus's twelve states — four labels times three commands — rest entirely on the unpinned enumeration. A verifier working only from what this artifact pins can confirm the 21, the commands and the rssProtocol, and can confirm nothing about which four machines, what hardware, or which UDID.
shouldFix.notAnInvention: Stated plainly because it bears on severity: the specs are correct. All four labels reproduce byte-for-byte against the adopted D-102 hosted-fleet-class contract as recorded at G03 v4's fleetClass. Nothing here is fabricated. The defect is that the corpus's own pins do not reach the content it carries.
shouldFix.theFamilyAlreadySolvedThis: The sibling g03-input-corpus.v1 does the identical job and does it correctly: it pins G03 v4, whose .harness.fleetClass holds the four labels, and its fleet states cite 'G03 v4 exactByteIntent and fleetClass' — naming the field that actually holds them — with the added clause 'This catalog does not invent a machine identifier outside D-102.' The pattern was available, is one line of basedOn away, and was not followed. That is what makes this a defect rather than a house style.
shouldFix.severityReasoning: SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker. Nothing is invented, no obligation closes, no boundary moves, and no unlawful act is enabled — G04 stays unexecuted, DR-101 unsatisfied, OBL-2 open. But 75 percent of the corpus's fixture-shaping content sits outside its custody chain while its source fields point at two fields that do not contain it, and my closest precedent is the SHOULD-FIX I filed on the G03 harness for leaning on a parent whose standing its own pins could not establish. Severity is not raised to blocker on scale alone when the content checks out at source.
shouldFix.suggestedRepair: Add harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4.json (or the adopted D-102 fleet-class contract) to basedOn with its digest and a role naming it as the fleet-class source, and change the twelve source fields to cite that document's fleetClass field alongside G04 v1's exactByteIntent — matching what g03-input-corpus.v1 already does.

whatIsCorrectInThisArtifact.why: A REJECT on one finding should not leave the rest unmeasured, and the repair should not disturb what already holds.
whatIsCorrectInThisArtifact.occupancyPinIsRight: The hardest question in this subject is which G04 occupancy is live, and the corpus gets it right. Three G04 harness files exist. v1 is the artifactPathWhenAuthored occupancy and carries an independent ACCEPT at 0/0 whose recorded subject digest is the 568218d7 this corpus pins. v3 carries an independent REJECT at 1 blocker, CLAUDE-G04H-V3-B1, which charged that v3's authorityClaim falsely claimed to occupy artifactPathWhenAuthored because v1 already occupied it. The corpus's 'G04 v3 is not this pin (CLAUDE-G04H-V3-B1)' and its role line 'Live G04 occupancy. artifactPathWhenAuthored.' are both accurate against those bytes. v2 exists, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with no review on disk and no fleetClass, and is correctly left unmentioned.
whatIsCorrectInThisArtifact.claimPhrase: classMemberVerbatim on all sixteen states is 'Baseline/peak RSS is bounded', byte-equal to G04 v1's claimVerbatim.
whatIsCorrectInThisArtifact.theOtherFourStatesTrace: The two rssProtocol states, the outside-D-006 state and the D-006 numerals state all trace to the fields they cite. '/proc/T/status VmRSS (kB) * 1024 = bytes per sample' and 'sample every 10 ms from the D-102 exec handshake to T exit' are in linuxPrimitive; 'task_info(T, TASK_VM_INFO) resident_size bytes per sample', 'same 10 ms window' and 'PROC_PIDARCHINFO is not used' are in macosPrimitive, with 'APIs are those on MacOSX15.4.sdk' compressed to 'APIs on MacOSX15.4.sdk'; the outside state's two halves are in threshold.explicitlyOutside and failsIf, both cited; '40/50/60/100 MB' and 'raw bytes are retained' are in rssProtocol.unit.
whatIsCorrectInThisArtifact.prohibitionsHold: Zero SATISFIED and zero QUALIFIED. No binary-MB byte constant: I searched for 41943040, 52428800, 62914560, 104857600, 1048576 and 1000000 and found none, and the only conversion present is the kB-to-bytes 1024 quoted from linuxPrimitive. No D-006 unit is invented — the D-006 state records the numerals as UNDECIDED pending the unit successor, which is rssProtocol.unit's own posture. Analyze and consented-probe RSS are recorded as not scored, matching threshold.explicitlyOutside and failsIf. Three leftover-join mentions and two OBL-2 mentions, all refusals; no occupancy join is invented and none exists on disk. One Rosetta mention, a refusal, grounded in G04 v1's failsIf. Three DR-G04 and one DR-G* refusal, zero pipe characters, so no row markdown. All sixteen states NOT-AUTHORED with zero fixture paths among the three quoted paths. Bare integers 1, 10, 21, 26 and 1024 all account to the version, the sampling window, the trace count, required-now and the kB conversion; only 4, 7 and 16 do not, and those are the finding.

independence.priorParticipation: This is the sharpest independence exposure of the session and I am stating it before the finding rather than after. The corpus's central decision — pin v1, disclaim v3 — rests entirely on two verdicts I authored: the CLAUDE-G04H-V3-B1 blocker that rejected v3, and the ACCEPT that made v1 live. The subject cites my finding ID by name. I re-derived that question from the live bytes of all three occupancy files rather than from my own verdicts, and confirmed independently that v1 sits at the artifactPathWhenAuthored path the harness itself names.
independence.theRiskThisCycle: Two risks pulled in opposite directions. Having authored the blocker the subject relies on, I had an interest in finding the subject sound. And having accepted the last two corpora, I risked reading a third the same way. What broke both was checking where content lives rather than whether it looks right: the fleet labels read as obviously legitimate, and they are legitimate — they simply are not in anything this corpus pins, which only a provenance search shows.
independence.howTheFindingWasReachedNotAssumed: I did not infer the gap from the citation text. I enumerated G04 v1's complete path list, searched its full serialization for every label and spec, read both cited fields in full, then located the labels by repository-wide search and byte-compared them against G03 v4's fleetClass. The sibling comparison came last and confirmed the pattern the corpus departed from.
independence.residualRisk: I set the standard this family is measured against, in the G16 verdict, and have now applied it eight times across four rejections and four acceptances. The line between this SHOULD-FIX and the advisory I filed yesterday on G15's AT-3 citation is mine: there the content sat one field away inside a pinned document, here it sits outside the custody chain entirely. A reviewer who had not drawn that line would be better placed to test it.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 1 SHOULD-FIX, 0 blockers. Twenty-four attacks run; twenty-three refuted. Custody holds throughout: subject e97f5634 at 0444, 12177 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified; all three cited pins reproduce, and the artifact's three 64-hex strings and three quoted paths are the same three. That small pin set is where the finding lives. Twelve of the sixteen states open with one of four fleet labels carrying specific hardware and a machine UDID — macos-15 (arm64, 3-core, 7 GB), macos-15-intel (native Intel VM, UDID 4203018E-580F-C1B5-9525-B745CECA79EB), ubuntu-24.04 (x64, 4 CPU, 16 GB), ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64, 4 CPU, 16 GB). None of the four appears anywhere in G04 v1. I enumerated that file's complete path list: it has no fleetClass field and no fleet label at any depth, and its only fleet reference is matrix, which reads 'same D-102 fleet class' and nothing further. All twelve states cite 'G04 v1 exactByteIntent and matrix', and I read both cited fields in full — neither contains a label. The corpus pins G04 v1, its review and file 08, and pins neither G03 v4 nor D-102, so no document in its custody chain carries the content. The count depends on it as well: exactByteIntent says 'Per platform' without saying how many platforms, so twelve states of four labels by three commands rest entirely on the unpinned enumeration, and three of the eight bare integers in the file exist only inside those specs. This is a custody gap, not an invention, and I say so plainly: all four labels reproduce byte-for-byte against the adopted D-102 hosted-fleet-class contract as recorded at G03 v4's fleetClass. Nothing is fabricated, no obligation closes, DR-101 stays unsatisfied and OBL-2 stays open. What makes it a defect rather than a house style is that the family already solved this — the sibling g03-input-corpus.v1 does the identical job, pins G03 v4 whose fleetClass holds the four labels, and cites 'G03 v4 exactByteIntent and fleetClass', naming the field that actually holds them. The repair is one basedOn entry and twelve source strings. Everything else in the artifact holds, including the hardest question in it: which G04 occupancy is live. Three G04 harness files exist, and the corpus pins the right one — v1 sits at the artifactPathWhenAuthored path the harness itself names, carries an independent ACCEPT at 0/0 whose recorded subject digest equals the pin, while v3 carries a REJECT at CLAUDE-G04H-V3-B1 for claiming that same occupancy, and v2 is unreviewed and correctly unmentioned. The class phrase is byte-equal to claimVerbatim on all sixteen states; the four non-fleet states trace to the fields they cite; no binary-MB byte constant appears under any of six searched forms; no D-006 unit is invented; analyze and consented-probe RSS are recorded as not scored; no occupancy join is invented and none exists. Disclosure, stated before the finding rather than after: the corpus's pin choice rests on two verdicts I authored, and it cites my blocker ID by name. I re-derived that question from the live bytes of all three occupancy files rather than from my own verdicts. The fleet labels read as obviously legitimate, and they are — they simply are not in anything this corpus pins, which only a provenance search shows.
